speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with a generalized nonpruritic rash, a recent high fever, and a seizure. To understand the cause of these symptoms, have you noticed any specific changes in your behavior, such as irritability, sleep disturbances, or memory loss in the days leading up to the fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum). The classic presentation of high fever (>40.5°C) resolving or present with the onset of a generalized nonpruritic rash in a 9-month-old infant, followed by a seizure due to fever, is highly characteristic of this condition caused by Human Herpesvirus 6 or 7.
